speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a young patient presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; can you tell me exactly when these symptoms first appeared and how the pain feels?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Septic Arthritis of the left wrist (suspected Lyme disease or gonococcal arthritis).

I have noted your recent camping trip in Minnesota and the self-resolving knee pain, which raises concern for disseminated Lyme disease; I also need to rule out gonococcal arthritis given your sexual activity. Please confirm if the skin lesions are itchy or painful, and REQUEST TEST: CBC, CRP, ESR, WBC count, Blood culture, and Syphilis/Chlamydia testing.
